messages.subject: negative chisq (even when method = "satorra.bentler.2010")

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: negative chisq (even when method = "satorra.bentler.2010")
parts: When comparing the models (with anova / lavTestLRT), I get a negative chi2...

That implies your constrained-loadings model fits better, which means your models must not be nested.  Looking at your scripts, I have a hard time seeing why.  You are using lavaan 0.6-5, so the latent variances should have been freed in the second group once you constrained loadings to equality.  Using the semTools::net() function, I cannot get the configural model to converge when fitting it to the model-implied moments from the equal-loadings model.  Maybe there is an identification / convergence issue that lavaan is not detecting...
I've seen that using method = "satorra.bentler.2010" should avoid this

Only when you use a robust estimator (e.g., MLR or MLM, requiring raw data), but your models still have to be nested, so the above issue would still be a problem. 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: negative chisq (even when method = "satorra.bentler.2010")
parts: But they should be nested, right? From the code I'm using I can't see why they wouldn't be...
Me neither.
So you think this has something to do with this specific data? And that generally this shouldn't happen?

That is my best guess.  The configural model fits so poorly (and surprisingly, worse than the metric-invariance model) that I wonder whether the optimizer found a local solution that is way off out there compared to the solution found for the (also poorly fitting) metric model.  But I would still expect that the configural model should be able to fit perfectly to any model-implied covariance matrix from a more constrained metric-invariance model (that is what nesting means).

I tried empirically checking whether your models are identified.  The configural model passes the empirical check: Fitting that model to its own model-implied covariances results in finding the same solution (and thus fits perfectly).

cov_fit1 <- sapply(fitted(fit1), "[[", i = "cov", simplify = FALSE)
update(fit1, sample.cov = cov_fit1, se = "none")

The metric invariance model does not pass this check, nor can the configural model find a solution for the metric model's model-implied Sigmas:

cov_fit2 <- sapply(fitted(fit2), "[[", i = "cov", simplify = FALSE)
update(fit2, sample.cov = cov_fit2, se = "none") # can't reproduce its own solution
update(fit1, sample.cov = cov_fit2, se = "none") # neither can the configural model

The only identification issue I thought of was that you have a 2-indicator factor, but even constraining those 2 loadings to equality does not resolve the issue.

mod <- '

## latent variable definitions (CFA)
ADHD =~ adhd1 + adhd2 + adhd3
IQ =~ c(L1, L2)*iq1 + c(L1, L2)*iq2

ANX =~ anx1 + anx2 + anx3
ADHD ~ IQ + ANX
IQ ~~ ANX
'

fit1 <- cfa(mod,
            sample.cov = cov_list,
            sample.nobs = c(150,150),
std.lv = TRUE, meanstructure = FALSE,

group = "gender")
fit2 <- cfa(mod,
            sample.cov = cov_list,
            sample.nobs = c(150,150),
            std.lv = TRUE,

group = "gender", meanstructure = FALSE,
            group.equal = "loadings", constraints = "L1 == L2")
lavTestLRT(fit1, fit2)

So I would just blame this anomaly on very poor data-model correspondence.

Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: negative chisq (even when method = "satorra.bentler.2010")
parts:
Mattan S. B.:
  Here are a few additional observations for what they are worth.

1. You appear to be analyzing correlations as if they were covariances.  This is not recommended.
2. I would recommend analyzing measurement invariance with a CFA model rather than, as you did, a structural model.
3. I would recommend using the CFA() function only for CFA models.
4. If you look at the correlation matrices, they are not what one would expect for homogeneous measures.  There is considerable heterogeneity in correlations across items on the same putative scale.  Moreover, these patterns seem to vary across groups.
5. Note the warning that your fit2 did not converge to a proper solution in group 1.

  My guess is that your measurement model is not well specified in one or both groups and that even if it were, it would not be invariant across groups.  My suggestion would be to go back a step to fitting the model separately in each group.  My guess is that your measures of the same construct are heterogeneous and do not all fit a common factor model.  Unfortunately, with so few measures, you cannot test this independently for each scale.  You may have to treat the eight observed variables as separate variables in a path analysis.  You could still test equality of structural parameters across groups.

Keith
------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.
http://www.routledge.com/books/details/9781841692203/

I noticed that Model 1 does not converge without std.lv = TRUE.

In lavaan dev 0.6-6,
lavTestLRT(fit1, fit2, method = "satorra.bentler.2010")

in this example will issue two warnings:

Warning in lavTestLRT(fit1, fit2) :
lavaan WARNING: method = "satorra.2000"
but no robust test statistics were used;
switching to the standard chi-square difference test

Warning in lavTestLRT(fit1, fit2) :
lavaan WARNING: some restricted models fit better than less
restricted models; either these models are not nested,
or the less restricted model was stuck in a local optimum.

Let me know if you feel the wording could be improved.

Yves.
